wikiGoal:
# Benchmark documentation brief

Create a source-grounded wiki for engineers who must understand, operate, debug, and safely change this repository.

- Explain the architecture, ownership boundaries, core data/control flows, persistence, external integrations, configuration, and failure handling.
- Include a practical quickstart and focused change guides for representative maintenance tasks.
- Treat source code and tests as authoritative. Cite concrete source evidence for every non-obvious technical claim.
- State uncertainty when the repository does not establish a fact. Do not invent runtime behavior, guarantees, or deployment details.
- Prefer a coherent, non-overlapping taxonomy over exhaustive file-by-file narration.

pages.title: Agent Host runtime
pages.purpose: The utilityProcess that embeds pi-coding-agent: RPC server, session wrappers, tool definitions, model runtime, and toolchain execution.
instructions: Describe AgentSessionWrapper: queueing, events, extension binding, external channel turns, idle eviction
Describe handler registration and main-process request forwarding (callMain) including channelSecrets and managed process registrations
Describe model catalog refresh coordination and offline fallback
Document the host entrypoint and lifecycle messages (ping, attach-port, toolchain/browser snapshots, shutdown)

pages.title: Architecture and process model
pages.purpose: Three-process Electron architecture: Main, Agent Host utilityProcess, and Renderer; ownership boundaries and core data/control flows.
instructions: Document Host supervision, crash restart budget, ping liveness, and snapshot ack flows from host-manager.ts
Explain how MessagePorts bridge renderer-to-host and how main mediates host requests
Explain no-local-server design principle and data persistence in ~/.pi/agent/
Ground each process role in concrete entrypoints with line references
